messages:
michael: spinning up ivy-9B (quant q4_0) for onboarding smoke on runtime-stable-3. short repro: coherent until ~380 tokens then it repeats the last sentence and KV cache size ramps steadily. suspect rotary/RoPE or kv index misalign with int4 kernels. anyone seen this pattern? :thinking:

anika: can you paste the minimal request + logs? helpful to see the exact runtime flags and model metadata (rope base, freq ordering, tensor layout). also which quant tool/version?

michael: here — request config + excerpted logs:
```
POST /v1/generate
model: ivy-9b
quant: q4_0
runtime: runtime-stable-3
max_tokens: 4096
input_len: ~48

Model metadata: rope_scaling: none, rope_mode: rotary, src_rope: legacy

LOGS:
[1723456791] kv_cache_size_bytes=0
[1723456795] kv_cache_size_bytes=1536000
[1723456805] kv_cache_size_bytes=3276800
[1723456840] kv_cache_eviction=1
[1723456841] generated: "...and that's why the project succeeded."
[1723456842] generated: "and that's why the project succeeded."
[1723456843] generated: "and that's why the project succeeded."

sample output attached as text file (repeats after ~384 tokens)
```

priyaa: hmm, two quick hypotheses: 1) rotary frequency table ordering changed between our quant kernel and the model export (freq indexing offset causes attention to attend to wrong positions -> repetition), 2) kv-index pointer/stride mismatch for int4 storage leading to partial overwrites (eviction flags look suspicious). did you use the new in-memory packing for q4?

deploy-bot: runtime-stable-3 deployed at 1723456770 (commit: abc123f). rolling update included q4 kernel optimizations and new kv packing. :rocket:

tom: i can repro locally on my devbox with dynamic batch=1. got the same repeat at token ~390. quick workaround that fixed it for me: set runtime flag `--legacy-rope-ordering=true` and disable the new q4 packer. after that behavior disappeared (still need perf check).

eva: ran quick evals against fp16 baseline on the same 120-sample prompt set: avg ppl +3.2 when using q4_0 on stable-3, and two prompts produced looping/rep output. also noticed BLEU-ish metric dropped on a few structured tasks. attaching small eval diff.

anika: concrete next steps: 1) priyaa, can you validate the rotary freq table ordering between model.ckpt metadata and runtime (pack/unpack)? add a small unit test that compares per-head rotation coefficients. 2) michael, rerun quantize with the flag `--preserve-rope-ordering` (newer quantizer has this) and attach new artifacts. 3) tom, please capture a token-level kv dump (positions, head offsets) for the failing run and upload. 4) eva, hold perf/regression evals on this runtime until we confirm kv/roation fix. mark P1 for onboarding blocker if root cause looks like runtime mismatch. :eyes:

priyaa: i pulled the model headers quickly — model exported with rope_base=10000 and ordering=interleaved (legacy expects contiguous). runtime-stable-3's q4 packer currently writes interleaved->packed with an index permutation that assumes contiguous ordering. that mismatch will cause per-head rotation to be applied incorrectly. i can prototype a converter by EOD to remap the freq table during model load.

michael: thanks — i pushed the failing sample + kvcache dump here: https://redwood.internal/s3/ivy9b/failing-smoke-1723456789.tar.gz (contains kvcache.hdump and sample-gen.txt). i've pinned routing to fp16 for now in the catalog.

tom: confirmed priyaa's repro locally by remapping freq table on load — repetition disappears and outputs align with fp16 baseline. good catch. we should add a runtime check that validates rope ordering at model load and emits a warning/error.

anika: agreed. priyaa, please open a runtime PR with: a) loader remapping helper, b) a unit test using small synthetic rotary table (covers both orderings), c) an opt-in env var `REDWOOD_FORCE_ROPE_REMAP` (default off until we land tests). michael, keep the model pinned in catalog and update onboarding ticket with link to this thread.

priyaa: will do. i'll also add a small perf note — remapping adds ~0.8ms cold-start overhead for large models but negligible steady-state.

michael: perfect. thanks everyone. tagging @eng-runtime and @eng-infra for visibility. i'll remove the pin once we verify nightlies. :thumbsup:
